plans.name: The farmhouse
plans.idea: Two squads with both LMG and the 9-1 hold the upper floor of the farmhouse O6-P6 in the centre, on the road to the middle exit: a fire base that sees most of the German setup area and draws the Germans toward it while the battalion enters behind.
plans.givesUp: All five counters and the best leader stand in one wooden building two hexes from the German setup area, and the Germans move first with eight squads; the flanks are not watched from the ground.
terrain: O6 and P6 are wooden building hexes with a level 1 and a stairwell each.
From level 1, P6 sees 47 of the 83 hexes numbered 8 to 10 on board 4, from A9 to GG10, and O6 sees 33; from the ground P6 sees 12.
O8, P8, and Q8 are at range 2 of P6, and Q9, O9, and N8 at range 3.

A wall runs along the west and south sides of the yard hexes O7 and P7, directly south of the farmhouse (hexsides O7-N6, O7-N7, O7-O8, P7-O8, and P7-P8). From P6's ground level it blocks the LOS to the south-west, to A9 for one; from level 1 the LOS passes over it, which is why the plan stands upstairs.
Board 4 is level ground. The Germans set up in its hexes numbered 8 to 10 after seeing the five counters, and move first, before the other fifteen British counters enter along the north edge.
The exit hexes lie ten hexes south of board 4's last hexrow: 2Y1 below 4I10, 2Q1 below 4Q10, and 2I1 below 4Y10 (board 2 is reversed).

plans.name: West woods
plans.idea: A squad with an LMG at the south edge of the woods H5-H6-I5-I6 and a squad with a 2-in. mortar and an 8-0 deeper in them cover the western route, by the dirt road I1-I2-I3-H3 toward the exit below 4I10; the mortar may fire Smoke for the crossing (SSR 3).
plans.givesUp: Nothing east of hexrow Q is seen, so the Germans may shift there unseen; the 9-1 and one LMG stay with the main body, the woods give less cover than a building, and from I5 the mortar sees little, so it must move up to H6 before it can lay Smoke on the German area.
terrain: H5, H6, I5, and I6 are woods; I1, I2, I3, and H3 are dirt road hexes leading to them from the north edge.
H6 sees 32 of the 83 hexes numbered 8 to 10 on board 4, all from A9 to Q10: G8, H8, and I8 at range 2, E8 and G9 at 3.
I5 sees only 9 of them, K8 at range 4 the nearest, each through a hindrance of 2 to 4.
The Studio's LOS counts grain as a hindrance; the card's date is May, when grain is not in season, so the hindered lines here are at least this open.
Board 4 is level ground. The Germans set up in its hexes numbered 8 to 10 after seeing the five counters, and move first, before the other fifteen British counters enter along the north edge.
The exit hexes lie ten hexes south of board 4's last hexrow: 2Y1 below 4I10, 2Q1 below 4Q10, and 2I1 below 4Y10 (board 2 is reversed).

plans.name: Two posts
plans.idea: One squad with an LMG watches from the upper floor of the farmhouse and one with an LMG and an 8-0 from the woods at H6, eight hexes apart: between them they see the German setup area from A9 to GG10, and the Germans cannot tell which route the battalion will take.
plans.givesUp: Each post is one squad that cannot help the other, and the farmhouse squad has no leader to rally it.
terrain: From level 1, P6 sees 47 of the 83 hexes numbered 8 to 10 on board 4, from A9 to GG10; O8, P8, and Q8 are at range 2.
H6 is woods and sees 32 of them, all from A9 to Q10: G8, H8, and I8 at range 2.
H6 and P6 are eight hexes apart.

A wall runs along the west and south sides of the yard hexes O7 and P7, directly south of the farmhouse (hexsides O7-N6, O7-N7, O7-O8, P7-O8, and P7-P8). From P6's ground level it blocks the LOS to the south-west, to A9 for one; from level 1 the LOS passes over it, which is why the plan stands upstairs.
The Studio's LOS counts grain as a hindrance; the card's date is May, when grain is not in season, so the hindered lines here are at least this open.
Board 4 is level ground. The Germans set up in its hexes numbered 8 to 10 after seeing the five counters, and move first, before the other fifteen British counters enter along the north edge.
The exit hexes lie ten hexes south of board 4's last hexrow: 2Y1 below 4I10, 2Q1 below 4Q10, and 2I1 below 4Y10 (board 2 is reversed).

plans.name: Storm the farmhouse
plans.idea: The Germans move first, and the farmhouse holds two squads and the best British leader, alone until the battalion enters. Three squads and the 9-2 wait behind the house at P8, three squads and the 8-1 behind the woods at M8, and two squads with the 9-1 fire from the woods at R8: the house is attacked from the south and the west in the first German turn, before help can reach it.
plans.givesUp: Nothing stands east of hexrow R or west of hexrow L, so both flank roads are open; if the farmhouse holds through the first turn, the battalion enters behind eight squads that are all in the centre.
terrain: P9 has no LOS to or from the upper floor of the farmhouse, O6 or P6: the house at P8 blocks it. It is three hexes from P6 and one from the road hexes Q9 and Q10.
L8 has no LOS to or from the upper floor of O6 or P6: the woods at M8 block it. It is four hexes from O6.
R8 is woods and sees the upper floor of P6 at range 3; O6 does not see it.
Neither P9 nor L8 is seen by the farmhouse, so each stack may take a "?" once both sides have set up (A12.12).
The exits are on board 2, ten hexes south of board 4's last hexrow: 2Y1 below 4I10 (the west), 2Q1 below 4Q10 (the centre), and 2I1 below 4Y10 (the east).

plans.name: Seal the west road
plans.idea: The British post in the woods at H6 and I5 marks the west road as the battalion's way. Three squads and the 9-2 in the woods at K9 fire on H6 and block the road south of it, a squad holds the house at I10 where the west road leaves board 4, two squads and the 9-1 start unseen at N8 to come at the woods from the east, and two squads with the 8-1 behind the house at P8 keep the centre road.
plans.givesUp: The east third of the board is empty, and the centre is two squads; the K9 stack is in the LOS of the squad at H6 from the start.
terrain: K9 is woods and sees H6 at range 4 through a hindrance of 3, and the road hex I9 at range 2; I5 does not see it.
I10 is a wooden building; it sees H6 at range 4 and I9 at range 1.
N8 has no LOS to or from H6 or I5: the woods at M8 block both. It is six hexes from H6.
P9 has no LOS to or from H6 or I5, and sees the centre road at Q9 and Q10 at range 1.
Neither N8 nor P9 is seen by the British post, so each stack may take a "?" once both sides have set up (A12.12).
The Studio's LOS counts grain as a hindrance; the card's date is May, when grain is not in season, so the hindered lines here are at least this open.
The exits are on board 2, ten hexes south of board 4's last hexrow: 2Y1 below 4I10 (the west), 2Q1 below 4Q10 (the centre), and 2I1 below 4Y10 (the east).

plans.name: Both posts
plans.idea: Each British post is one squad, and the two cannot help each other. Three squads and the 9-2 behind the house at P8 go for the farmhouse, three squads and the 9-1 in the woods at K9 go for the woods at H6, and two squads with the 8-1 wait unseen in the woods at T9 to turn east or centre once the battalion shows its route.
plans.givesUp: The force is in three parts from the start, and only the reserve of two squads covers the east road; the K9 stack is in the LOS of the squad at H6.
terrain: P9 has no LOS to or from the upper floor of P6, nor H6: the house at P8 and the woods at M8 block them. It is three hexes from P6.
K9 is woods and sees H6 at range 4 through a hindrance of 3; the farmhouse does not see it.
T9 is woods; neither post sees it. It sees the centre road at Q9 and Q10 at range 3 and Y10, where the east road leaves board 4, at range 5.
Neither P9 nor T9 is seen by a British post, so each stack may take a "?" once both sides have set up (A12.12).
The Studio's LOS counts grain as a hindrance; the card's date is May, when grain is not in season, so the hindered lines here are at least this open.
The exits are on board 2, ten hexes south of board 4's last hexrow: 2Y1 below 4I10 (the west), 2Q1 below 4Q10 (the centre), and 2I1 below 4Y10 (the east).

plans.name: Three roads
plans.idea: One group stands in a building on each way south, whatever the five British counters show: three squads and the 9-2 in the house at P8 on the centre road, two squads and the 8-1 in the house at I10 where the west road leaves board 4, two squads and the 9-1 in the house at X8 and a squad in the house at Y9 where the east road leaves board 4.
plans.givesUp: No group is strong enough to attack the British posts in the first turn, and the three cannot help each other quickly: the Germans wait for the battalion to choose its road.
terrain: P8 is a wooden building; it sees the centre road at Q9 at range 1 and Q10 at range 2, and the upper floor of the farmhouse sees it at range 2 to 3.
I10 is a wooden building where the west road leaves board 4; it sees I9 at range 1. Only a post at H6 sees it, at range 4.
X8 and Y9 are wooden buildings; they see Y10, where the east road leaves board 4, at range 2 and 1. The farmhouse, H6, and I5 do not see them.
X8 and Y9, and I10 unless H6 is held, are out of every British LOS, so their stacks may take a "?" once both sides have set up (A12.12).
The exits are on board 2, ten hexes south of board 4's last hexrow: 2Y1 below 4I10 (the west), 2Q1 below 4Q10 (the centre), and 2I1 below 4Y10 (the east).
